entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 61:1-8 . Neginah --or, Neginoth (see on Ps 4:1 , title). Separated from his usual spiritual privileges, perhaps by Absalom's rebellion, the Psalmist prays for divine aid, and, in view of past mercies, with great confidence of being heard.

entries.heading: 2. heart is overwhelmed
entries.text: 2. heart is overwhelmed --literally, "covered over with darkness," or, "distress." to the rock -- ( Ps 18:2; 40:2 ). higher than I --which otherwise I cannot ascend.

entries.heading: 3. shelter . . . and strong tower
entries.text: 3. shelter . . . and strong tower --repeat the same sentiment.

entries.heading: 4. I will abide
entries.text: 4. I will abide --So I desire to do (compare Ps 23:6 ). trust in the covert, &c.-- make my refuge, in the shadow (compare Ps 17:8; 36:7 ).

entries.heading: 5. the heritage
entries.text: 5. the heritage --or, part in the spiritual blessings of Israel ( Ps 21:2-4 ). vows --implies prayers.

entries.heading: 6, 7. the king
entries.text: 6, 7. the king --himself and his royal line ending in Christ. Mercy and truth personified, as in Ps 40:11; 57:3 .

entries.heading: 7. abide before God
entries.text: 7. abide before God --literally, "sit as a king in God's presence," under His protection.
8. Thus for new blessings will new vows of praise ever be paid.
